items.title: Signal Now Blocks AI Screen Access to Protect Chats
items.summary: Signal is extending screenshot-blocking protections to iPhones and supported Android devices to prevent AI assistants such as Siri and Gemini from capturing private conversations. In its announcement , Signal said AI assistants can capture messages displayed on screen, potentially exposing conversat…
items.body: Signal is extending screenshot-blocking protections to iPhones and supported Android devices to prevent AI assistants such as Siri and Gemini from capturing private conversations. In its announcement , Signal said AI assistants can capture messages displayed on screen, potentially exposing conversations to processing outside the app. End-to-end encryption protects message delivery, but cannot prevent another app from reading messages visible on a recipient's device. On iPhones running iOS 27 , the new "Block ‌Siri‌ AI" setting is enabled by default in Signal version 8.37 or later. It blocks screenshots, screen recordings, and AI screen-reading. On supported Android devices running Signal 8.35.1 or later, screen security activates when an AI assistant attempts to read the screen. iPhone users can disable the protection under Signal's Settings → Privacy → Block Siri AI , either permanently or for 10 minutes to take a screenshot. Apple also offers an Excluded Apps setting under Settings → Siri that prevents ‌Siri‌ from accessing selected apps. Signal previously blocked Microsoft's Recall from capturing chats on Windows 11. It said equivalent screenshot blocking is unavailable on macOS and recommends excluding Signal from ‌Siri‌ there. The company is asking Apple, Google, and Microsoft for better tools to keep app content out of AI systems. items.title: Things 3.25 for Mac Gains Touch Gestures
items.summary: Cultured Code today released Things 3.25 for Mac, bringing full optimization for the PROLED MacBook Pro to its task management app. Since the touchscreen MacBook Pro launched, all Mac apps feature basic touch input, with taps performing the equivalent of mouse clicks. Things already worked with that…
items.body: Cultured Code today released Things 3.25 for Mac, bringing full optimization for the PROLED MacBook Pro to its task management app. Since the touchscreen MacBook Pro launched, all Mac apps feature basic touch input, with taps performing the equivalent of mouse clicks. Things already worked with that default behavior, but Cultured Code says version 3.25 fully optimizes the app for touch with additional gestures, improved dragging, and larger controls. A rightward swipe on a to-do opens the scheduling dialog, while a leftward swipe selects or deselects it. Users can also select several items by moving two fingers up or down through a list. To open a to-do, users can tap it to select it and tap again to expand it, or double-tap. Cultured Code says dragging to-dos and headings is smoother and more responsive, whether moving one item or a group. Holding a finger on an item in a selection picks up the whole group, rather than only that item. The update also improves how dragging works when some selected items are outside the visible area of the list. Custom menus and date pickers adapt to the input method, showing more spacious rows and larger touch targets when opened with a finger. Buttons elsewhere in the app also have larger tap targets. Other changes make it easier to resize the sidebar by touch and rearrange checklist entries within a to-do. Users can cancel either a to-do or an individual checklist entry by pressing and holding its checkbox. The release also includes smaller adjustments to touch interactions and interface polish throughout the app. Things 3.25 for Mac is available now.
